basis: Skeletal dysostosis with obligate intellectual disability (100%), a defining syndrome feature. Damaging ocular, hearing and dental findings are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: obligate intellectual disability (100%) is a defining feature of this dysostosis syndrome.

basis: Defining intellectual disability/myopathy; dental malocclusion 4/6 and LV systolic dysfunction 2/6. Sleep apnea does not establish direct lung or airway injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: sleep apnea in 2/2 assessed patients does not establish direct pulmonary or airway damage; no independent respiratory lesion is documented.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental malocclusion and incisor macrodontia each affect 4/6 (67%); teeth and their structural abnormalities belong to this axis.

basis: Peroxisomal metabolic defect; neurologic disease in most, hepatic and retinal injury commonly >=30%. Common hearing loss omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurologic dysfunction affects most patients across the spectrum; the PEX10 umbrella is defined by its peroxisomal metabolic defect.

basis: Pleural tumour origin; direct invasion of chest-wall or diaphragmatic muscle is common (approximately >=30%) over its usual locally progressive course.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: the definition describes progression into chest-wall muscle; direct muscle invasion is common, approximately >=30% over the typical disease course.

basis: Catecholamine synthesis defect causing cardiovascular and autonomic dysfunction; decreased GFR 2/2. Anemia 2/2 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia in 2/2 qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining autonomic dysfunction and renal functional impairment.
decisions.neurologic: primary: inherited failure of autonomic noradrenergic neurotransmission defines the orthostatic disorder and represents neurologic loss of function.

basis: Inherited methemoglobin disorder; aggregate nervous-system abnormalities are frequent (30-79%), with direct CNS injury in generalized reductase deficiency. Cyanosis is not skin damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: aggregate nervous-system HPO frequency is 30-79%; developmental and structural CNS injury support damage, although individual findings are occasional.

basis: Bilateral optic nerve sheath tumours; the optic nerve is explicitly included in the ocular axis. No separate brain or other neurologic involvement is specified.

decisions.neurologic: none: optic nerve and its local sheath tumour are assigned to ocular; meningioma histology alone does not establish additional neurologic organ involvement.

basis: Congenital myopathy with defining Robin oral anomalies and impaired ocular abduction; ptosis 6/8. Facial weakness is myopathic; independent global developmental delay is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.neurologic: none: facial weakness and motor delay arise from congenital myopathy; independent global developmental delay is occasional (5-29%), without common nerve/CNS injury.

basis: Immune-complex vasculitis with defining skin disease; neuropathy ~50-60% (HPO 30-79%). Renal injury ~30%, GI infarction and arthritis (HPO 30-79%) omitted by cap; viral hepatitis is separate.

decisions.renal: none: renal injury qualifies (HPO 30-79%, usually about 30%), but more prevalent neuropathy and defining skin disease take the remaining slots.
decisions.neurologic: involved: direct peripheral neuropathy is common, roughly 50-60%, consistent with the supplied frequent (30-79%) HPO annotations.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: vasculitic purpura is part of the defining triad; skin ulcers in 80-99% confirm direct cutaneous injury.

basis: Glycosylation defect with platelet/neutrophil abnormalities; pulmonary hemorrhage HPO 80-99%. Neurodevelopmental impairment affects most later reported cases (>30%); small cohorts.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and encephalopathy occur in most later reported cases (>30%); the single-case definition is incomplete.
